questions.q: 56. While drawing straight lines, the general direction of the movement of pencil or pen is from
questions.explain: For a right-handed person, drawing left to right prevents the hand from smudging the freshly drawn line.

questions.q: 57. Bisecting a line means to divide it into
questions.explain: To 'bisect' geometrically means to cut something precisely into two equal halves.

questions.q: 58. The angle between two perpendicular lines is
questions.explain: By definition, perpendicular lines meet at an exact right angle of 90 degrees.

questions.q: 59. The angle between two horizontal lines is
questions.explain: Two horizontal lines are parallel to each other, and therefore the angle between them is 0 degrees.

questions.q: 60. Dashed line in drawing generally indicate
questions.explain: Dashed (hidden) lines are the standard convention used to represent edges or surfaces that are not visible from the current viewing angle.

questions.q: 61. Continuous thick lines generally represent
questions.explain: Solid, continuous, thick lines are used to define the visible outline and edges of an object.

questions.q: 62. Unseen edge of a shape in orthographic view is shown by
questions.explain: Standard drafting convention uses dashed lines to indicate edges that are hidden behind other surfaces of the object.

questions.q: 63. The space between two words while lettering should be approximately equal to the
options: half the width of a letter
questions.explain: To maintain readability and proportion, the gap between words is generally set to the width of a single average letter.

questions.q: 64. In ......... dimensioning method, all dimensions are placed so that they may be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet.
questions.explain: Unidirectional dimensioning is a system where all text, regardless of the dimension line's orientation, is oriented horizontally to be read from the bottom of the sheet.

questions.q: 65. In ........... dimensioning method, dimensions are placed perpendicular to the dimension line
questions.explain: In the aligned method, the dimension text is oriented in line with the dimension line so it reads correctly from the bottom or the right side of the sheet.

questions.q: 66. The main purpose of lettering in a drawing is to give
options: information which cannot be conveyed by lines
questions.explain: Lettering provides notes, dimensions, and specifications that cannot be visually represented purely by the object's geometric lines.

questions.q: 85. The lines used to draw a machine drawing according to their thickness are called
questions.explain: Standard drawing lines (thick, thin, dashed, etc.) with specific meanings assigned to them are collectively known as conventional lines.

questions.q: 86. Leader line is used to give
questions.explain: A leader line is a thin line ending in an arrowhead used to connect a note or dimension text directly to the specific feature it describes.

questions.q: 87. Section lines/Hatching lines are generally drawn at
questions.explain: The standard convention for hatching (cross-hatching) to indicate a cut/sectioned material is a 45-degree angle to the main outlines.

questions.q: 88. Horizontal lines are generally drawn from
questions.explain: Following the standard drafting convention, horizontal lines are drawn from left to right using a T-square or parallel bar.

questions.q: 89. Vertical lines are generally drawn from
questions.explain: Vertical lines are typically drawn from the bottom of the sheet upwards toward the top using a set square resting on the T-square.

questions.q: 105. The slant of the letters written in slant style makes an angle of ....... with the horizontal.
questions.explain: Slanted (italic) lettering in technical drawing conventionally uses a 75-degree angle from the horizontal for legibility and standardization.

questions.q: 106. The ratio of height to width of the letters and numerals should normally be kept as
questions.explain: Standard lettering proportions maintain a height-to-width ratio of 5:3 for optimal readability.

questions.q: 154. A ...... is a thin line used to indicate a feature to which a number, note or dimension applies.
questions.explain: By definition, a leader line points from an annotation to the specific part of the drawing it refers to.

questions.q: 171. Dimension line and projection line (extension line) are drawn as
questions.explain: To distinguish them from the object's visible outline (thick lines), dimension and extension lines are drawn as thin continuous lines.
